# Adjie Brotosukmono

> Adjie Brotosukmono is an Indonesian senior economics consultant and power system engineer at Mott MacDonald in Perth, Western Australia, and a Professional Member of Engineers Australia. Adjie holds a Bachelor's in Electrical Power Engineering and a Master's in Electrical Engineering from Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), and has also worked in banking and online education.

Canonical site: https://www.adjiebrotots.com/
Full story: https://www.adjiebrotots.com/about/
Projects, in detail: https://www.adjiebrotots.com/projects/
Also known as: Harso Adjie Brotosukmono (full name), Adjie Brotot (nickname), adjiebrotot (handle)
Based in: Perth, Western Australia, Australia. Citizen of Indonesia, resident of Australia.
Languages: Bahasa Indonesia (native), English (full professional); elementary Chinese, Japanese, Russian and French
Contact: adjiebrotots@gmail.com, https://www.linkedin.com/in/adjiebrotot/

## Who Adjie is, in short

- Current role: Senior Economics Consultant at Mott MacDonald in Perth. Commercial and technical work: project and bid management, strategic advisory for the energy industry, techno-economic modelling and power system analysis, for miners, system operators and renewable developers, mostly in Western Australia.
- Specialties: security-constrained economic dispatch, connection studies, techno-economic analysis for investment decisions, market forecasting, and custom simulation software (Python, C, C++). Tools: DIgSILENT PowerFactory, PSCAD, PSS/E.
- Grid codes: WEM Rules and WEM Procedures (Western Australia's SWIS), Pilbara Network Rules, NWIS Harmonised Technical Rules, and some NEM experience.
- Mentors graduate engineers and interns to build energy models from scratch.
- Professional Member of Engineers Australia.
- Education: Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), Indonesia. Bachelor of Science in Electrical Power Engineering; Master of Science in Electrical Engineering. Master's research: "Optimal Scheduling Algorithm for Coal-Powered Power Plants: Considering Coal Delivery Constraints".

## Career, in order (no dates on purpose)

1. University at ITB, Bandung. Academic assistant (power system engineering lab coordinator; lab assistant for power system analysis and high voltage; assistant lecturer for signals and systems, electrical materials, electromagnetics). Founded Ganeshtore, a supply store for new students. Production engineering internship at LG Electronics. Research engineer at E-Life Solutions Sdn. Bhd. in Johor, Malaysia, on ERMA, electromagnetic risk management software. Youth programmes: Scholarion Exchange (Japan), ASEAN Young Leaders Program (Singapore, Cambodia), Young ASEAN Leaders Policy Initiative (Thailand, twice), 30th International Youth Forum (Seoul), and the Hult Prize Manila Regionals (Philippines) with a university team. Awards: finalist, Electrical Engineering Competition; semifinalist, Electrical Engineering Competition, Tour, and Rally; first place in debate, logo and video (NESCO) competitions.
2. Teaching: academic coach at Quipper, physics teacher at Pahamify (@fisikaambis), then Academic Lead, a project manager role. Freelance teaching for university and high school students for years.
3. A one-month role as software engineer at CAD-IT Consultants (ASIA), building an IoT monitoring app with ThingWorx.
4. Product Manager for credit cards at PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BCA), Jakarta: led credit card digital features with business analysts, developers and testers; worked with Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB and UnionPay. Projects: contactless cards including BCA Card contactless, CVV/CVC in the app, in-app payments and virtual card numbers (myBCA, klikBCA, BCA mobile), tokenisation for Visa, Mastercard and JCB, and BCA's issuer wallet with tap-to-pay using host card emulation.
5. Power System Engineer at Merz Consultancy Pty Ltd (Perth, working from Jakarta), continuing at Mott MacDonald after Merz merged with it, still from Jakarta. Projects: essential system services (ESS) headroom study for Pilbara ISOCo in the NWIS (showed headroom procurement could drop from 200 MW to 60 MW; the report became the basis of the procurement); Darwin-Katherine Electricity System generation portfolio optimisation for the NT Department of Mining and Energy (economic basis of the Detailed Business Case for the Darwin Renewable Energy Hub); power factor correction for Bluestone Mines Tasmania at Renison Bell (capacitor bank now in operation); harmonic filter design for TransAlta St Ives Wind Farm and Cunderdin Solar Farm, and a transformer energisation EMT study for St Ives; the Energy Balancing and Settlement (EBAS) engine for Pilbara ISOCo (first project as Project Manager, still in use); Collgar Wind Farms constraint study; lead developer of EGPO (generation portfolio optimiser) and WEMulator (WEM dispatch engine emulator). Other studies: Quenda Wind Farm, APA Wallumbilla Compressor Station, Norton Gold Fields, TransAlta Mt Keith, Blue Power Engineering wind farm pre-feasibility, Formosa 2 Wind Farm (Taiwan), a PSCAD and PSS/E scripting package for NEM connection studies, and technical support to Energy Policy WA on the Power System Security and Reliability Standards framework.
6. Economics Consultant at Mott MacDonald in Perth. Projects: the next round of the Pilbara ISOCo ESS headroom study as acting Project Manager (report used for the ESS procurement); synchronous condenser placement and optimisation for PWR Hybrid's Mount Magnet operations; completing the Darwin-Katherine optimisation.
7. Now Senior Economics Consultant at Mott MacDonald in Perth: acting Project Manager on power system studies, client contact and bid manager. Projects: the third round of the Pilbara ISOCo ESS headroom study as Project Manager; Red Gully BESS (BLT Energy) and Paterson BESS (TagEnergy) connection work; the NWIS under-frequency load shedding incident investigation; the NWIS Access and Connection Guideline; grid connection strategy for GreenWind's Ambrosia and Mahogany Wind Farms; solar PV and tariff advice for DevelopmentWA's Australian Marine Complex. The Perth role was advertised locally first, as Australian law requires, and asked for a power system engineer with banking and finance experience.
